In the devdesk Go repo (TUI app, Bubble Tea), I need to understand the configuration system to plan a new `dk setup` wizard command that interactively creates/overwrites a named "context" config file.

Please investigate and report back (concise, with file paths and line numbers):
1. `internal/config/config.go` — the full `Config` struct schema (all fields, nested structs like `App`, forge settings, network/docker settings, scan settings, etc.), and what fields have a closed set of valid values (look for functions like `ContainerEngines()`, `config.EngineAuto` etc., theme lists, secret backend options).
2. How contexts are stored on disk: where context YAML files live (look for `~/.devdesk/`, context file naming, `internal/config` functions like `Load`, `Save`, `List contexts`, `Switch context`, path resolution, default context).
3. `applyDefaults` function in config.go — what defaults get applied.
4. Any existing CLI flag/arg parsing in `main.go` (does it use `flag`, `cobra`, or something custom? how are subcommands like potential `dk setup` currently dispatched, if any exist already, e.g. `dk version`, `dk --help`).
5. Any existing "wizard" or interactive prompt patterns elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. bubbletea forms used outside the TUI, or a survey/prompt library in go.mod).
6. The forge config section — what are the two backends (gitlab, github?) and what fields does each need (mentioned in forge.md doc)? Check `docs/architecture/forge.md` and `internal/config` for forge-related struct fields.
7. Secret backend options (`app.secret_backend`: auto, keyring, git-credential) — where declared.
8. Migration handling (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`) mentioned in CLAUDE.md — is there existing migration code style to mimic for a "create config from scratch" flow.

Report concisely: struct definitions (trimmed to relevant fields), function signatures with file:line, and any closed-value-set helper functions with their exact names. This is read-only research — do not write any code.

59	// nowhere to carry the string, which is the guarantee `context_get` already

62		// Enabled decides whether the TUI serves at all. The refusal names this
63		// setting and the context, because activating it in the wrong one is
64		// otherwise an hour spent looking at a server that will not start.

67		// Expose is an **allow-list** of tool names; empty means every declared
68		// tool. It is not a deny-list, for the reason §3.38 gives in the other
69		// direction: a tool never registered cannot fail to be excluded, whereas a
70		// deny-list is one forgotten line away from exposing what arrives next.
71		Expose []string `yaml:"expose,omitempty"`

74		// because that is both the most closed bind available and the one that

77		// the LAN ever being offered the port. The sandbox's own network policy is
78		// a second lock — the port has to be allowed there by name.

81		// configurability: on native Linux Docker `host.docker.internal` does not
82		// reach the host's loopback, and the bridge gateway would have to be bound
83		// instead. That case does not exist here and is not handled — but a literal
84		// would have to be rewritten, where a setting has to be documented.
85		//
86		// An empty value means the default, never "listen nowhere": the zero value

394	// applyDefaults applies the default values to a configuration.
395	// Returns an error when the file cannot be normalized — today
396	// only for registries (duplicate slug, missing parent group).
397	func applyDefaults(cfg *Config) error {
398		homeDir, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
399	
400		// `gitlab:` → `forge:`, and it runs **first**. That is not tidiness: every
401		// default below writes into cfg.Forge, so a migration placed after them
402		// would find a block that is no longer empty and take the field-by-field
403		// path — where every field is already filled with a default, and the user's
404		// own `parallel_jobs: 7` is silently dropped. Measured, not theorised: it
405		// is what the first draft did, and the retired-keys test caught it.
406		//
407		// The other half of the reason is `docker:` → `network:`'s: yaml.Unmarshal
408		// is not strict here, so an un-migrated block is dropped in silence, and the
409		// silence would point a context at no host at all.
410		migrateGitLabSection(cfg)
411	
412		// "dark" was a third name for the built-in theme: LoadTheme accepts "",
413		// "dark" and "default" alike, but ListThemes only ever offers "default", so
414		// a config saying "dark" named a theme no picker could show. Normalised at
415		// load; LoadTheme still accepts the old name for a file not yet rewritten.
416		if cfg.App.Theme == "" || cfg.App.Theme == "dark" {
417			cfg.App.Theme = "default"
418		}
419		if cfg.App.LogFile == "" {
420			cfg.App.LogFile = filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "devdesk.log")
421		}
422		if cfg.App.DefaultView == "" {
423			cfg.App.DefaultView = "dashboard"
424		}
425		if cfg.App.WorkspacesDir == "" {
426			cfg.App.WorkspacesDir = filepath.Join(homeDir, "workspaces")
427		}
428		if cfg.App.IDECommand == "" {
429			cfg.App.IDECommand = "code"
430		}
431		// Left empty, credentials.Select already treats this as "auto"; naming it
432		// keeps the setting inside the closed set the configuration view cycles
433		// through, so the first arrow press does not jump somewhere arbitrary.
434		if cfg.App.SecretBackend == "" {
435			cfg.App.SecretBackend = "auto"
436		}
437		// Same reason: engine.Resolve reads "" as auto, but the configuration view
438		// cycles a closed set and a value outside it has nowhere to start from.
439		if cfg.App.ContainerEngine == "" {
440			cfg.App.ContainerEngine = EngineAuto
441		}
442		if cfg.Status.RefreshInterval == 0 {
443			cfg.Status.RefreshInterval = 10
444		}
445		if cfg.Status.Timeout == 0 {
446			cfg.Status.Timeout = 5
447		}
448		if cfg.Forge.Type == "" {
449			cfg.Forge.Type = ForgeGitLab
450		}
451		if cfg.Forge.DefaultVisibility == "" {
452			cfg.Forge.DefaultVisibility = "private"
453		}
454		if cfg.Forge.CloneMethod == "" {
455			cfg.Forge.CloneMethod = "https"
456		}
457		if cfg.Forge.Pull.ParallelJobs == 0 {
458			cfg.Forge.Pull.ParallelJobs = 4
459		}
460		if cfg.Registry.CacheDir == "" {
461			cfg.Registry.CacheDir = filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "cache", "templates")
462		}
463		// Migrate old single-registry config to the new Registries list
464		if cfg.Registry.URL != "" && len(cfg.Registry.Registries) == 0 {
465			cfg.Registry.Registries = []RegistryItem{{
466				URL:      cfg.Registry.URL,
467				Username: cfg.Registry.Username,
468				AuthMode: AuthCredentials,
469			}}
470		}
471		if cfg.Scan.CacheDir == "" {
472			cfg.Scan.CacheDir = filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "cache", "scans")
473		}
474		if cfg.Scan.MaxCachedReports == 0 {
475			cfg.Scan.MaxCachedReports = 50
476		}
477		if cfg.Scan.Timeout == 0 {
478			cfg.Scan.Timeout = 300
479		}
480		if cfg.Scan.MaxConcurrentScans == 0 {
481			cfg.Scan.MaxConcurrentScans = 3
482		}
483		// An address the file does not carry is the default, never "nowhere":
484		// a bind that silently does not happen would look exactly like a server
485		// that is off, and `mcp.enabled` is what answers that question.
486		if cfg.MCP.Listen == "" {
487			cfg.MCP.Listen = DefaultMCPListen
488		}
489	
490		// Auto is the historical resolution, so a config that predates the setting
491		// keeps behaving exactly as it did.
492		if cfg.Scan.TrivySource == "" {
493			cfg.Scan.TrivySource = ToolSourceAuto
494		}
495		if cfg.Scan.GitleaksSource == "" {
496			cfg.Scan.GitleaksSource = ToolSourceAuto
497		}
498		if cfg.Scan.PlumberSource == "" {
499			cfg.Scan.PlumberSource = ToolSourceAuto
500		}
501	
502		if cfg.Network.CheckTimeout == 0 {
503			cfg.Network.CheckTimeout = DefaultCheckTimeout
504		}
505		if cfg.Network.PingCount == 0 {
506			cfg.Network.PingCount = DefaultPingCount
507		}
508		if cfg.Network.CertExpiryWarnDays == 0 {
509			cfg.Network.CertExpiryWarnDays = DefaultCertExpiryWarnDays
510		}
511		if cfg.Network.PortsRefreshInterval == 0 {
512			cfg.Network.PortsRefreshInterval = DefaultPortsRefreshInterval
513		}
514	
515		// Backward compat: configs created before the scan-option booleans were introduced
516		// will have all of them at Go's zero value (false). Treat "all disabled" as
517		// "never configured" and apply sensible defaults so scans work out of the box.
518		//
519		// EnableCIScore is read here but never written below, and the asymmetry is
520		// the point. It is newer than the four, so a file that predates them has it
521		// false too and the migration still fires; but "the four off and CI on" is a
522		// deliberate configuration — the user asked for CI alone — and forcing vuln
523		// and secret back on would overwrite it on every load. Leaving it out of the
524		// condition is what a test caught.
525		if !cfg.Scan.EnableVuln && !cfg.Scan.EnableSecret && !cfg.Scan.EnableMisconfig &&
526			!cfg.Scan.EnableLicense && !cfg.Scan.EnableCIScore {
527			cfg.Scan.EnableVuln = true
528			cfg.Scan.EnableSecret = true
529		}
530	
531		// Last, so that the registry migrated from the legacy single-registry keys
532		// above gets a slug like every other one.
533		return normalizeRegistries(cfg.Registry.Registries)
534	}

728	func LoadContext(contextName string) (*Config, error) {
729		if err := ValidateContextName(contextName); err != nil {

731		}
732	
733		configPath, err := GetContextPath(contextName)
734		if err != nil {
735			return nil, err
736		}

738		// Check whether the file exists
739		if _, err := os.Stat(configPath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
740			return nil, fmt.Errorf("context '%s' does not exist (no file at %s)", contextName, configPath)
741		}
742	
743		// Read and parse YAML
744		data, err := os.ReadFile(configPath)
745		if err != nil {
746			return nil, err
747		}
748	
749		var cfg Config
750		if err := yaml.Unmarshal(data, &cfg); err != nil {
751			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse context '%s': %w", contextName, err)
752		}
753	
754		// Apply the default values
755		if err := applyDefaults(&cfg); err != nil {
756			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid context '%s': %w", contextName, err)
757		}
758	
759		// Expand paths (tildes)
760		if home, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil {
761			cfg.ExpandPaths(home)
762		}
763	
764		return &cfg, nil
765	}

767	// ExpandPaths expands tildes (~) in configuration paths
768	func (c *Config) ExpandPaths(homeDir string) {
769		expand := func(path string) string {
770			if strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") {
771				return filepath.Join(homeDir, path[2:])
772			}
773			return path
774		}
775	
776		c.App.LogFile = expand(c.App.LogFile)
777		c.App.WorkspacesDir = expand(c.App.WorkspacesDir)
778		c.Registry.CacheDir = expand(c.Registry.CacheDir)
779		c.Scan.CacheDir = expand(c.Scan.CacheDir)
780		c.Scan.TrivyPath = expand(c.Scan.TrivyPath)
781		c.Scan.GitleaksPath = expand(c.Scan.GitleaksPath)
782		c.Scan.GitleaksConfig = absolute(expand(c.Scan.GitleaksConfig))
783		c.Scan.PlumberConfig = absolute(expand(c.Scan.PlumberConfig))

786	// absolute pins a configured file path to one meaning.
787	//
788	// A relative gitleaks_config does not mean the same thing on both sides of the
789	// Docker boundary — DevDesk's working directory in binary mode, the container's
790	// in Docker mode — and the file is now mounted, so the two readings would
791	// disagree about which file is scanned with. Resolving it here settles it
792	// against DevDesk's own working directory, once, at load: the path that gets
793	// mounted and the path the configuration view shows are then the same string.
794	//
795	// A path that cannot be resolved is left as it was rather than dropped:
796	// RunGitleaks refuses an unreadable config with the reason, and that is a
797	// better place to fail than a config file that silently loses a setting.
798	func absolute(path string) string {
799		if path == "" {
800			return ""
801		}
802		abs, err := filepath.Abs(path)
803		if err != nil {
804			return path
805		}
806		return abs
807	}

57		if err != nil {
58			fmt.Printf("Warning: Could not create log file: %v\n", err)
59		} else {
60			defer func() { _ = logFile.Close() }()
61			log.Printf("=== DevDesk Started ===")
62			log.Printf("Config loaded from context: %s", getCurrentContextName())
63			log.Printf("Log file: %s", cfg.App.LogFile)
64			log.Printf("DEBUG mode: %v", len(os.Getenv("DEBUG")) > 0)
65		}
66	
67		// Load and apply the saved theme
68		if cfg.App.Theme != "" && cfg.App.Theme != "dark" {
69			t, err := theme.LoadTheme(cfg.App.Theme)
70			if err != nil {
71				log.Printf("Warning: Could not load theme '%s': %v, using default", cfg.App.Theme, err)
72			} else {
73				theme.ApplyTheme(t)
74				theme.CurrentThemeName = cfg.App.Theme
75				log.Printf("Theme loaded: %s", cfg.App.Theme)
76			}
77		}
78	
79		// Create the application with the router
80		m := app.New(cfg)
81	
82		// Bubble Tea program options
83		opts := []tea.ProgramOption{
84			tea.WithAltScreen(), // Full-screen mode
85		}
86	
87		// Start the Bubble Tea program
88		p := tea.NewProgram(m, opts...)
89	
90		// The router needs the handle before the loop starts: an MCP request
91		// reaches Update() through p.Send, and there is no other legal door
92		// (Rule 110). Written here, once, while nothing else is running.
93		m.AttachProgram(p)
94	
95		if _, err := p.Run(); err != nil {
96			fmt.Printf("Error running application: %v\n", err)
97			os.Exit(1)
98		}
99	}

3	// The container engine names. They are stated here as well as in
4	// internal/engine, and TestEveryConfiguredEngineHasAShape keeps the two in

6	// `provider` names have (§3.8). config must not import a backend, and a

1	package config
2	
3	// The forge vocabulary. It is stated here as well as in internal/forge, and
4	// TestTheForgeVocabularyMatchesTheBackends keeps the two in step — the same
5	// arrangement the registry `provider` names have between config and
6	// registrymgr (§3.8). A config value that no backend answers to would resolve
7	// to nothing at load, which is a failure mode worth a test rather than a
8	// comment.
9	const (
10		// ForgeGitLab is the default, and what every file written before `type:`
11		// existed means.
12		ForgeGitLab = "gitlab"
13		ForgeGitHub = "github"
14	)
15	
16	// ForgeTypes lists what `forge.type` accepts, in the order the configuration
17	// view cycles them.
18	func ForgeTypes() []string { return []string{ForgeGitLab, ForgeGitHub} }
19	
20	// migrateGitLabSection carries a legacy `gitlab:` block into `forge:`.
21	//
22	// Field by field, and only where the new value is empty: a file that already
23	// carries `forge:` keeps it, so a half-written file does not have its new
24	// values overwritten by its old ones. The legacy struct is cleared once read,
25	// so the key leaves the file on the next save — the precedent is
26	// RegistryItem.AuthEnabled and, right below this in applyDefaults,
27	// `docker.network_tool_image`.
28	//
29	// It runs **before** the defaults. yaml.Unmarshal is not strict here, so an
30	// un-migrated block is dropped in silence, and the silence would point a
31	// context at no host at all.
32	func migrateGitLabSection(cfg *Config) {
33		legacy := cfg.GitLab
34		if legacy == (GitLabConfig{}) {
35			return
36		}
37		defer func() {
38			// A legacy file predates `type:` by definition, so it can only mean
39			// GitLab. Cleared last, so the key leaves the file on the next save.
40			if cfg.Forge.Type == "" {
41				cfg.Forge.Type = ForgeGitLab
42			}
43			cfg.GitLab = GitLabConfig{}
44		}()
45	
46		// Nothing under `forge:` at all — the ordinary case, and the only one where
47		// a bool can be carried over safely: IncludeArchived's zero value *is*
48		// false, so no per-field guard could tell "unset" from "deliberately off".
49		if cfg.Forge == (ForgeConfig{}) {
50			cfg.Forge = ForgeConfig{
51				URL:                legacy.URL,
52				DefaultParentGroup: legacy.DefaultParentGroup,
53				DefaultVisibility:  legacy.DefaultVisibility,
54				CloneMethod:        legacy.CloneMethod,
55				Pull: ForgePullConfig{
56					ParallelJobs:    legacy.Pull.ParallelJobs,
57					IncludeArchived: legacy.Pull.IncludeArchived,
58				},
59			}
60			return
61		}
62	
63		// Both blocks are present, which a hand-edited file can be. The new one
64		// wins field by field: its values were written later, and overwriting them
65		// with the old ones would undo the edit that created the situation.
66		if cfg.Forge.URL == "" {
67			cfg.Forge.URL = legacy.URL
68		}
69		if cfg.Forge.DefaultParentGroup == "" {
70			cfg.Forge.DefaultParentGroup = legacy.DefaultParentGroup
71		}
72		if cfg.Forge.DefaultVisibility == "" {
73			cfg.Forge.DefaultVisibility = legacy.DefaultVisibility
74		}
75		if cfg.Forge.CloneMethod == "" {
76			cfg.Forge.CloneMethod = legacy.CloneMethod
77		}
78		if cfg.Forge.Pull.ParallelJobs == 0 {
79			cfg.Forge.Pull.ParallelJobs = legacy.Pull.ParallelJobs
80		}
81	}

1	# The forge abstraction, its vocabulary, and the explorer clone
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	## The forge abstraction — `internal/forge`
7	
8	What DevDesk asks of a code-hosting platform, so a context can target GitLab or
9	GitHub — exactly one, never two (§3.6). `internal/forge/gitlab` is the only
10	package that knows go-gitlab exists, `internal/forge/github` the only one that
11	knows go-github, and `internal/forge/session` the only one that knows both
12	exist.
13	
14	Five decisions hold it together, each forced by what the code consumes:
15	
16	| | |
17	|---|---|
18	| **Identity is opaque, the path is not** | `ID` addresses an object with the backend and means nothing outside — GitLab needs a number for `ParentID`, GitHub addresses by owner. `Path` is what the clone URL, the display and GitLab's renamed-path deletion are built from. The type is a string so arithmetic on it cannot be written; only the backend reads it back |
19	| **A namespace and a repository are different types** | only a namespace has children, only a repository has a CI status and a scheduled deletion. "Drill into a repository" is unexpressible rather than forbidden by review |
20	| **Decoration is an option** (`BrowseOptions.Decorated`) | the role and CI status cost two requests **per repository** on GitLab. The explorer asks; the clone's walk does not, which is what keeps a two-hundred-repository group from costing 400 calls for a badge nobody reads |
21	| **`Shape` is declared, never sniffed** | nesting depth, the visibility set, whether a delete can be permanent. `CanNestUnder` reads the "unbounded" sentinel in one place — the obvious comparison refuses the *root* namespace on GitHub, where the maximum is 1 |
22	| **`DashboardStats` counters are `*int`** | five independent requests, any of which fails on its own. `nil` means nobody looked (D52) |
23	
24	Two properties come with the seam: **the backend paginates** and no caller ever
25	sees a page (D34), and **every call takes a context**, which is what the clone's
26	cancellable discovery needs and `context.Background()` everywhere prevented.
27	
28	`CurrentUser` is **memoised** on the backend. Every decorated listing needs the
29	caller's id for its role lookups, and asking the host each time would add a
30	request per listing that the pre-abstraction code did not make — it took the id
31	from a session the view was already holding. Who a token belongs to does not
32	change for the life of a session.
33	
34	**A decoration that fails does not fail the listing; a listing that fails is
35	never an empty list.** Both directions have a test. It is one rule seen from two
36	sides: a column short beats an empty explorer, and an empty explorer must never
37	mean "this group contains nothing".
38	
39	**`internal/forge/session` opens sessions, and it is the one place that knows
40	both backends exist.** `internal/forge` must not import an implementation and a
41	backend must not import its sibling, so something above both has to choose:
42	`session.Backend(forgeType, url, token)` is that switch, and an unknown type
43	falls through to GitLab — `applyDefaults` has already normalised the value, and
44	the one backend that has always existed beats an error nothing can act on.
45	
46	The credential store is **not** forge-shaped: `Storage` is keyed on a URL and
47	knows nothing else, so loading and forgetting a token are the same code either
48	way. Only opening a session differs, and only in which constructor it calls —
49	which also means a context that switches platform without changing host finds
50	the token it already had, and that is right, because it is the same host asking.
51	
52	**GitHub refuses what it cannot express, rather than doing something
53	adjacent.** There is no REST endpoint for creating or deleting an organisation
54	— both come back as errors naming the reason, where the tempting alternative
55	would be creating a repository under the user's own account and calling it an
56	organisation. A permanent delete is refused for the same reason: GitHub deletes
57	at once, so honouring the flag would report a distinction the platform does not
58	make, and `Shape.PermanentDelete` is false so the checkbox is never offered.
59	
60	**An initial commit is one commit, and that is why it is four calls.**
61	`Repositories.CreateFile` in a loop makes one commit per file, so a three-file
62	template would arrive as three — and each would need the SHA the last returned,
63	which is a chain rather than a batch. The git data API takes it at once: a blob
64	per file, one tree, a commit with **no parent**, then the ref. No parent is what
65	makes it *initial*; on a repository that already has one the ref creation fails,
66	which is the honest outcome — this is not a way to overwrite history.
67	
68	Three smaller decisions worth knowing:
69	
70	- **The user's own account is the first root namespace, and leaving it out was
71	  a bug.** The reasoning that excluded it — "a personal namespace cannot be
72	  created or deleted, so half the actions would refuse the row" — is wrong on
73	  its own terms: *no* GitHub organisation can be created or deleted through the
74	  API either, so the personal account is not less capable but **more**. It is
75	  the one namespace where a repository can be created and deleted. The cost was
76	  the common case: a personal account belongs to no organisation, so the
77	  explorer opened empty on the account shape most people have. Its `ID` is the
78	  **empty string** — the interface's own word for "the user's own namespace",
79	  and what `Repositories.Create` takes for its `org` argument; the login would
80	  404, because GitHub refuses to treat a user as an organisation. Its children
81	  come from `/user/repos` with `Affiliation: owner`, without which the list also
82	  carries every repository the user collaborates on — which belongs under
83	  whoever owns it, and would appear twice in a tree that shows both.
84	- **`visibilityOf` reads `Visibility` before `Private`.** The first is what
85	  Enterprise fills with `internal`; reading only the boolean would report an
86	  Enterprise `internal` repository as `private`, which is a different thing.
87	- **A running workflow reports its *status*.** A run in flight has no
88	  conclusion, and falling through to empty would make a repository whose build
89	  is running read as having no CI at all.
90	
91	The configured URL is the **web** host. On Enterprise the API lives under
92	`/api/v3/`, which `WithEnterpriseURLs` appends — conflating the two would send a
93	user to `https://git.acme.test/api/v3/acme/api` when they asked to open a
94	repository in a browser.
95	
96	**One rough edge, and §3.56 moved it rather than fixing it.** The explorer's
97	Type column read the vocabulary, so the personal account's row said
98	"Organization". GitHub calls the union "Owner", but taking that word into
99	`Vocabulary.Namespace` would make the configuration read "Default parent owner",
100	which is worse — and a third node kind would reintroduce the sum type the
101	two-types decision exists to avoid.
102	
103	The column is a glyph now, and a glyph belongs to no forge, so the table no
104	longer makes the claim at all. The words moved to the help's **Row Icons**
105	legend, where a sentence has room to be right — which is the whole reason
106	`nodeTypeLabel` survives the column that used to be its only caller. The rough
107	edge is still there, in the legend; it is simply not repeated on every row.
108	
109	Cost: **+0.55 MB** on the binary (24.4 → 25.0).
110	
111	Worth knowing: **go-gitlab retries 5xx** with an exponential backoff — a test
112	serving 500 took 35 seconds, measured. Not a regression (it is the SDK's
113	default), but an unreachable instance makes the user wait behind a spinner.
114	
115	## The vocabulary — `forge.Vocabulary`
116	
117	What a forge is **called**, as opposed to what it can do. The distinction is
118	§3.6's and it is the whole design: "Group" against "Organization" is a *word*,
119	while nesting depth and the visibility set are *shapes* — they change what the
120	application can promise, and no wording helps with them. `Shape` carries the
121	second, `Vocabulary` the first, and neither grows conditionals for the other.
122	
123	**Per forge, not neutral.** A GitLab user says *group*, a GitHub user says
124	*repository*; "namespace" is a third language nobody speaks and makes the
125	application read as an abstraction layer rather than as a tool. The *field
126	names* are neutral because the code has to be — a view cannot switch on which
127	forge it is talking to — but nothing a user reads is.
128	
129	**Resolved from the config, not from the session.** `forge.VocabularyFor(
130	cfg.Forge.Type)`, not a method on `Forge` and not a field on `shared.State`:
131	the explorer's "not authenticated" screen and the auth view's own title both
132	need the words *before* any session exists, so a value hanging off a live
133	backend would be missing exactly where it is needed most. Each view has a small
134	`vocab()` helper; the config is what every one of them already holds.
135	
136	**No view writes anything specific to one forge into a string, and a test says
137	so.** `internal/ui/vocabtest` parses every `.go` under `internal/ui` and fails
138	on a string literal containing a forge **marker** — import paths excluded, and
139	one declared exception (`theme.ForgeIcon`'s own switch), on the model of
140	`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`. A wording table nothing enforces drifts back one
141	message at a time, and the messages that drift are the ones nobody reads until a
142	GitHub context renders "GitLab not authenticated".
143	
144	The markers are the two **names** *and* the token **prefixes** (`glpat-`,
145	`ghp_`, `github_pat_`, …), and the second half was added after the first half
146	missed something. The auth view carried `glpat-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx` as its
147	token placeholder for the whole of §3.6, and this test walked past it every
148	time: a token prefix is forge-specific **without naming a forge**, which is
149	exactly the shape a guard on names cannot see. `Vocabulary.TokenPlaceholder`
150	carries it now — shaped like a real value, because that is what a placeholder
151	is, while the prose about which prefixes exist lives in `TokenHelp`, where there
152	is room to name more than one.
153	
154	**A command name is not vocabulary.** It is routing identity, the same for both
155	forges (§3.6 step 8 makes it `git-auth`), so a message quoting one builds it
156	from `command.ViewGitlabAuth` rather than writing it out. That is also what
157	makes the message survive the rename instead of quietly outliving it.
158	
159	**The icon is the theme's, keyed on the same constant.** `theme.ForgeIcon` and
160	`forge.VocabularyFor` are two tables because a domain package must not import
161	the UI — but both switch on `config.ForgeGitLab` / `config.ForgeGitHub` rather
162	than on a literal, so there is one spelling of "gitlab" in the application and a
163	new forge cannot be half-added.
164	
165	What is *not* in the vocabulary, and deliberately: the visibility set (a shape,
166	on `Shape`), the humanised role (the backend's, because GitLab's numbers and
167	GitHub's words do not align), and the token prefix as a *check* — it is a hint,
168	`TokenPlaceholder`, and DevDesk validates nothing, so saying "must" about it is
169	how a user comes to believe a working token is broken.
170	
171	Sites it took over: the explorer's title, its loading line, its empty and
172	signed-out screens, its Type column and its help; the auth view's title, help,
173	URL label and both "not configured" messages; the dashboard's Code box, its
174	tree root and its help; the configuration view's forge tab — its title, its
175	icon, its URL example and two field labels; and `CreationForm`'s two resource
176	types.
177	
178	
179	## The CI status vocabulary (D66)
180	
181	`Repository.CIStatus` is a **closed set of words, and it is GitLab's**:
182	`created`, `waiting_for_resource`, `preparing`, `pending`, `running`,
183	`success`, `failed`, `canceled`, `skipped`, `manual`, `scheduled`. They are
184	declared in `internal/forge/cistatus.go` and listed by `CIStatuses()`.
185	
186	The choice is historical rather than principled — GitLab was the only backend
187	when the field was added, so its own word went straight into the explorer's CI
188	column. Keeping it is still right: eleven values against GitHub's nine, and it
189	separates "queued" from "not started", so translating GitHub onto it loses less
190	than the reverse would.
191	
192	**A promise that only a comment made was not kept.** `lastWorkflowConclusion`
193	claimed to return "the same words the GitLab backend reports" and returned
194	GitHub's: of the nine outcomes Actions can produce, only `success` and `skipped`
195	happen to be spelled the same. `failure`, `cancelled` and `in_progress` reached
196	the CI column as raw text truncated to its six cells — `failu…`, `cance…`,
197	`in_pr…` — and, worse, coloured by `pipelineStatusStyle`'s default branch, which
198	is the **warning** style. A broken build read as a caution, in the one column
199	that exists to make a broken build obvious.
200	
201	Four GitHub outcomes have no counterpart and are folded rather than dropped,
202	each on its own argument:
203	
204	| GitHub | becomes | why |
205	|---|---|---|
206	| `timed_out`, `startup_failure` | `failed` | GitLab kills a timed-out job as `failed`; folding reports what GitLab would have |
207	| `action_required` | `manual` | a run waiting for an approval is exactly what GitLab calls manual |
208	| `neutral`, `stale` | `skipped` | GitHub renders both the way it renders skipped, and skipped is the only grey this set has |
209	| `queued`, `requested`, `waiting`, `pending` | `pending` | GitLab's four pre-run states differ to a scheduler, not to a reader |
210	
211	**An unrecognised value becomes the empty string, never itself.** That is what
212	`Repository.CIStatus` documents for a value a backend has no equivalent for, and
213	it is the difference between an empty cell and six characters of a platform's
214	internal spelling.
215	
216	**Two tests hold the contract, and neither existed before.**
217	`TestTheBackendOnlyEmitsDeclaredStatuses` walks the GitHub mapping tables and
218	refuses an output `CIStatuses()` does not declare;
219	`TestEveryDeclaredCIStatusHasAnIcon` walks the same list from the view and
220	refuses a status `pipelineStatusLabel` has no glyph for. The second is what
221	found the GitLab half of the defect: `created` and `scheduled` were missing from
222	that switch and printed their own names too.
223	
224	The view's `default:` branch survives both. It is unreachable for a backend that
225	keeps the promise, and it is what a backend that breaks it should hit — a
226	truncated word is a bad answer, and no answer at all is worse.
227	## The explorer table (§3.56)
228	
229	Eight columns, in this order: **icon, Name, Slug, Visibility, Role, CI, Created,
230	Activity**. Two of them are glyphs.
231	
232	The **first** carries the node kind and follows Rule 125 — untitled, two cells,
233	no comparator, no search key. It replaced a thirteen-cell `Type` column printing
234	"Group" or "Organization", and the eleven cells it returns go to Name and Slug,
235	the two columns that identify a row.
236	
237	**Visibility** is a glyph under its own whole word: a globe for public, a shield
238	for internal, a lock for private, and an **empty cell** for anything else — a
239	forge that grows a fourth value must not be shown one of the three that exist.
240	The word stays because it is what makes the three decodable without a legend,
241	and it costs nothing: the column is exactly ten cells, the width of its own
242	header. That is affordable only because the column **stopped sorting** — every
243	sortable column reserves two cells for an arrow, sorted or not
244	(`datatable/widths.go:askFor`), and three visibilities in an order nobody would
245	agree on were never a sort worth the width.
246	
247	The glyphs are deliberately none of the workspaces set. `ws` lists what is on
248	disk and `exp` lists what the forge holds; a row that looked the same in both
249	would claim they are the same object.
250	
251	**The table opens unsorted** (`SortColumn: -1`), which is not a change of
252	behaviour: `loadChildren` stacks namespaces then repositories, and the sort by
253	node type it replaced is the identity on that list. What is gained is that `.`
254	now has "no sort" as a stop, so the forge's own order is reachable again after
255	cycling away from it — a sort by type could never express that.
256	
257	## Creating and deleting — the row is the progress
258	
259	`N` and `D` are network calls, and the tree used to answer neither of them while
260	one was in flight. A create ran `handleRefresh()` on the way out: the table was
261	emptied and re-listed from scratch, so for the whole of the round trip the user
262	saw a blank body and a footer with nothing in it — and then the thing they had
263	asked for, with no thread connecting the two.
264	
265	**The row goes on screen when the request goes out.** `insertCreatingNode` puts
266	a `TreeNode{Creating: true}` at the level being browsed, keyed on the path
267	predicted from the parent and the slug; the spinner rides in the icon column
268	(`iconCell`), where the kind glyph will be. When the forge answers,
269	`settleCreating` swaps the placeholder for the real node **in place** — no
270	refresh, because the forge has just said what it made and re-listing the tree to
271	learn it would empty the table a second time. A failure takes the row away again
272	and says so in the footer.
273	
274	Three things follow, and each is the reason for a piece of the shape:
275	
276	| | |
277	|---|---|
278	| The path is a **prediction** | the row needs a key before there is an answer. The forge is free to differ, so `Target` travels on the message — it is the only thing that can still find the row that was put on screen |
279	| The spinner comes from the **broadcast** | this view's own chain stops on `!m.loading` (`handleSpinnerTick`), so a frame taken from it would freeze on frame zero the moment the tree settled. It is D5's argument, reached from the other side |
280	| The row is **inert** while it spins | `actionable()` refuses it, `GetShortcuts` greys `D`, and pressing the key says which of the two reasons applies (Rule 130). A placeholder carries no identifier, so an action addressing one would send an empty ID |
281	
282	Both are `jobs` runs (`KindCreate`, `KindDelete`) rather than a local flag — see
283	the jobs registry in [`app-shell.md`](app-shell.md) for why a single-item run
284	still earns one. The delete keeps its row and takes the same spinner: a row that
285	vanished before the answer came would be claiming something that has not
286	happened yet.
287	
288	## The explorer clone
289	
290	`C` in the explorer opens a **selection mode** over the same tree, and `enter`
291	starts a **pipeline** that discovers and clones at once (§3.16). It replaced a
292	single `Cmd` covering a whole subtree behind a modal reading `"Pulling..."` —
293	several minutes indistinguishable from a freeze on a large group.
294	
295	The line that holds it together: **the explorer creates what does not exist,
296	workspaces reconciles what does.** A repository already on disk is skipped
297	untouched, so the explorer never needs to know what a dirty working tree is and
298	the per-row states collapse to five — queued, cloning, cloned, already there,
299	failed. Updating an existing clone is §3.17's `sync`, in workspaces.
300	
301	Those five states are where `jobs.ItemState` came from, and since §3.58 they
302	*are* it: this screen is the item level of a clone run (D3), rendering a record
303	the router owns rather than keeping one of its own.
304	
305	| Mode | Screen | Keys |
306	|---|---|---|
307	| `ModeSelecting` | the tree, with a checkbox in the icon column | `space` ticks, `←→` drill, `enter` confirms, `esc` cancels |
308	| `ModeCloning` | a flat list, one row per repository | `esc` cancels, then closes |
309	
310	**The selection is roots plus exclusions, never a list of repositories**
311	(`selection.go`). A positive list cannot be built when a group is ticked without
312	enumerating its children — the full API walk, run at selection time, which is
313	the freeze moved one screen earlier. "This group, minus these" needs to know
314	nothing about what the group contains, so a group nobody has expanded can still
315	be ticked, displayed with the right tri-state, and walked. It is the only
316	representation compatible with discovering as you clone.
317	
318	The **nodes** are kept separately, in `Model.selectionNodes`: the walk has to
319	start from one, and a root ticked three levels down is no longer on screen once
320	the user has come back up. The selection itself stays paths-only, which is what
321	lets it answer for paths nobody has fetched.
322	
323	**The check state travels on a row type.** `datatable` columns are built once in
324	`New` and close over nothing, so the table moved from `Model[*TreeNode]` to
325	`Model[explorerRow]` (`row.go`) — the `imageRow` pattern. The state must **not**
326	move into `datatable`: `SetItems` replaces the items on every drill-down, while
327	the selection spans levels the table has never shown. `RenderCheckboxTri` styles
328	its output and so cannot go in a cell; `checkboxIcon` is the glyph without it
329	(Rule 122).
330	
331	The checkbox **rides on the icon cell** rather than taking a column of its own.
332	A column would cost four cells on every screen to say nothing on all but one of
333	them, and at 80 columns the explorer has none to spare.
334	
335	Since §3.56 that cell is two wide (Rule 125), so the checkbox and the kind glyph
336	cannot sit side by side — the box replaces the glyph. **What keeps the sharing
337	honest is the colour**: `iconStyle` paints `theme.IconRoleNamespace` or
338	`theme.IconRoleRepository` in both modes, so a ticked row still says group or
339	repository by hue. That is the one thing the icon-colour roles were added for,
340	and it is why they are not decoration.
341	
342	### The clone is a run of the registry (§3.58, D3)
343	
344	`cloneList` used to hold five states, a slice of rows, an index keyed on the
345	path and a spinner frame of its own. That was the fifth bookkeeping beside the
346	four `internal/jobs` replaced — and the one the plan named as the prototype to
347	generalise, because it was already a jobs view for a single kind.
348	
349	It renders the run now, and owns none of it:
350	
351	| | |
352	|---|---|
353	| the rows | `jobs.Run.Items`, from the snapshot the router broadcasts |
354	| the frame | the router's one chain (D5), taken bare — a table cell is measured before it is styled (Rule 122) |
355	| "finished" | `Run.Finished()`, not a flag this screen sets |
356	| the mapping | `CloneEventMsg.Transition()` — the clone's own vocabulary, in the clone's package, which is what `jobs.Reporter` exists for |
357	
358	**A clone run is *open***, and it is the only kind that is. Every other launch
359	site knows its full target list when it dispatches, which is what makes "8
360	waiting" sayable (D10); the clone's walk *is* what finds them, so
361	`jobs.NewOpenRun` registers a run with none and `Registry.Discover` adds each as
362	the walk turns it up. An open run is **never finished** whatever its items say —
363	a walk that has found three repositories and cloned all three is still going,
364	and settling it there would stop the spinner and print a summary the next
365	repository contradicts. `CloneRunFinishedMsg` seals it, through `jobs.Sealer`: a
366	second interface because a closed channel names no target.
367	
368	What this buys is the thing D3 asked for: **`:jobs` shows the same clone the
369	explorer is rendering**, without either copy being authoritative and without the
370	explorer having to be on screen for its rows to keep moving.
371	
372	**Two cancellation scopes, and the distinction is the point** (`pipeline.go`).
373	`cloneRun.cancel` is a `context.CancelFunc` covering **discovery only** — HTTP
374	reads, which cancel safely. A `git clone` is never interrupted: a context that
375	kills one leaves half a repository on disk, which is exactly what this avoids.
376	So `esc` cancels the walk and the scheduler stops issuing work, the running
377	clones are awaited, and the footer says `Cancelling — 3 clones finishing`. A
378	second `esc` must not force.
379	
380	`esc` goes **through the registry** (`jobs.CancelOpenMsg`), which holds the
381	cancel function from the launch. Calling the pipeline's own would stop the walk
382	behind the record's back and leave `:jobs` claiming the run finished on its
383	own — the distinction `Run.cancelled` exists to keep. Cancelling also seals:
384	the walk that would have closed the run is precisely what was stopped, so
385	leaving it open would keep it unsettled for the life of the session.
386	
387	The message names a **kind**, not an identifier. A progressive run belongs to a
388	screen that owns the display while it goes, so there is one open clone at a
389	time and the view can name it without holding a `JobID` — the registry state D1
390	keeps out of views.
391	
392	`cloneWalkFailed` is a kind of its own: a group that cannot be listed gets a
393	failed row naming the **group**, because the repositories under it were never
394	discovered and no other row can stand for them.
395	
396	The **failures are named when the run ends**, in the footer and the log. The
397	list is discarded on `esc` and workspaces records only the successes — a clone
398	that failed wrote nothing, so that report is the only one there will be.
399	
400	`gitlab.pull.include_archived` is read by `listGroupChildren` and **only by the
401	clone**: browsing lists everything the forge has.
402	
403	**A clone may never prompt, and `gitlab.Clone` is where that is enforced.**
404	Sending git's streams to the null device does not prevent a credential prompt —
405	it prevents git asking *itself*, after which the **credential helper** takes
406	over, and a helper is a separate process. Git Credential Manager writes
407	`info: please complete authentication in your browser` to the console directly,
408	over the top of the rendered frame, then waits. Bubble Tea cannot recover a
409	frame something else has written into: two frames end up visible at once, and
410	the row spins with nothing on screen saying why. Observed, not theorised.
411	
412	So `cloneEnv` shuts every interactive path — `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`,
413	`GCM_INTERACTIVE=never`, both askpass hooks, ssh in `BatchMode` — and the token
414	DevDesk already holds is passed as `http.extraHeader` **through the
415	environment**: argv is readable from the process list, and the `user:token@host`
416	URL form is written into every cloned repository's `.git/config` and stays
417	there. A stalled transfer is bounded by `http.lowSpeedLimit`/`lowSpeedTime`
418	rather than by killing the process, so git cleans up after itself and decision
419	12 still holds.
420	
421	The consequence to keep in mind: with the helper out of the loop, a context
422	whose stored token is missing or under-scoped **fails** rather than falling back
423	to a browser. That is the intended trade — a failed row naming git's reason
424	beats a spinner that never resolves — but it makes the token the only way in.
425

# The forge abstraction, its vocabulary, and the explorer clone

> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
> read this file when working on the code it describes.

## The forge abstraction — `internal/forge`

What DevDesk asks of a code-hosting platform, so a context can target GitLab or
GitHub — exactly one, never two (§3.6). `internal/forge/gitlab` is the only
package that knows go-gitlab exists, `internal/forge/github` the only one that
knows go-github, and `internal/forge/session` the only one that knows both
exist.

Five decisions hold it together, each forced by what the code consumes:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Identity is opaque, the path is not** | `ID` addresses an object with the backend and means nothing outside — GitLab needs a number for `ParentID`, GitHub addresses by owner. `Path` is what the clone URL, the display and GitLab's renamed-path deletion are built from. The type is a string so arithmetic on it cannot be written; only the backend reads it back |
| **A namespace and a repository are different types** | only a namespace has children, only a repository has a CI status and a scheduled deletion. "Drill into a repository" is unexpressible rather than forbidden by review |
| **Decoration is an option** (`BrowseOptions.Decorated`) | the role and CI status cost two requests **per repository** on GitLab. The explorer asks; the clone's walk does not, which is what keeps a two-hundred-repository group from costing 400 calls for a badge nobody reads |
| **`Shape` is declared, never sniffed** | nesting depth, the visibility set, whether a delete can be permanent. `CanNestUnder` reads the "unbounded" sentinel in one place — the obvious comparison refuses the *root* namespace on GitHub, where the maximum is 1 |
| **`DashboardStats` counters are `*int`** | five independent requests, any of which fails on its own. `nil` means nobody looked (D52) |

Two properties come with the seam: **the backend paginates** and no caller ever
sees a page (D34), and **every call takes a context**, which is what the clone's
cancellable discovery needs and `context.Background()` everywhere prevented.

`CurrentUser` is **memoised** on the backend. Every decorated listing needs the
caller's id for its role lookups, and asking the host each time would add a
request per listing that the pre-abstraction code did not make — it took the id
from a session the view was already holding. Who a token belongs to does not
change for the life of a session.

**A decoration that fails does not fail the listing; a listing that fails is
never an empty list.** Both directions have a test. It is one rule seen from two
sides: a column short beats an empty explorer, and an empty explorer must never
mean "this group contains nothing".

**`internal/forge/session` opens sessions, and it is the one place that knows
both backends exist.** `internal/forge` must not import an implementation and a
backend must not import its sibling, so something above both has to choose:
`session.Backend(forgeType, url, token)` is that switch, and an unknown type
falls through to GitLab — `applyDefaults` has already normalised the value, and
the one backend that has always existed beats an error nothing can act on.

The credential store is **not** forge-shaped: `Storage` is keyed on a URL and
knows nothing else, so loading and forgetting a token are the same code either
way. Only opening a session differs, and only in which constructor it calls —
which also means a context that switches platform without changing host finds
the token it already had, and that is right, because it is the same host asking.

**GitHub refuses what it cannot express, rather than doing something
adjacent.** There is no REST endpoint for creating or deleting an organisation
— both come back as errors naming the reason, where the tempting alternative
would be creating a repository under the user's own account and calling it an
organisation. A permanent delete is refused for the same reason: GitHub deletes
at once, so honouring the flag would report a distinction the platform does not
make, and `Shape.PermanentDelete` is false so the checkbox is never offered.

**An initial commit is one commit, and that is why it is four calls.**
`Repositories.CreateFile` in a loop makes one commit per file, so a three-file
template would arrive as three — and each would need the SHA the last returned,
which is a chain rather than a batch. The git data API takes it at once: a blob
per file, one tree, a commit with **no parent**, then the ref. No parent is what
makes it *initial*; on a repository that already has one the ref creation fails,
which is the honest outcome — this is not a way to overwrite history.

Three smaller decisions worth knowing:

- **The user's own account is the first root namespace, and leaving it out was
  a bug.** The reasoning that excluded it — "a personal namespace cannot be
  created or deleted, so half the actions would refuse the row" — is wrong on
  its own terms: *no* GitHub organisation can be created or deleted through the
  API either, so the personal account is not less capable but **more**. It is
  the one namespace where a repository can be created and deleted. The cost was
  the common case: a personal account belongs to no organisation, so the
  explorer opened empty on the account shape most people have. Its `ID` is the
  **empty string** — the interface's own word for "the user's own namespace",
  and what `Repositories.Create` takes for its `org` argument; the login would
  404, because GitHub refuses to treat a user as an organisation. Its children
  come from `/user/repos` with `Affiliation: owner`, without which the list also
  carries every repository the user collaborates on — which belongs under
  whoever owns it, and would appear twice in a tree that shows both.
- **`visibilityOf` reads `Visibility` before `Private`.** The first is what
  Enterprise fills with `internal`; reading only the boolean would report an
  Enterprise `internal` repository as `private`, which is a different thing.
- **A running workflow reports its *status*.** A run in flight has no
  conclusion, and falling through to empty would make a repository whose build
  is running read as having no CI at all.

The configured URL is the **web** host. On Enterprise the API lives under
`/api/v3/`, which `WithEnterpriseURLs` appends — conflating the two would send a
user to `https://git.acme.test/api/v3/acme/api` when they asked to open a
repository in a browser.

**One rough edge, and §3.56 moved it rather than fixing it.** The explorer's
Type column read the vocabulary, so the personal account's row said
"Organization". GitHub calls the union "Owner", but taking that word into
`Vocabulary.Namespace` would make the configuration read "Default parent owner",
which is worse — and a third node kind would reintroduce the sum type the
two-types decision exists to avoid.

The column is a glyph now, and a glyph belongs to no forge, so the table no
longer makes the claim at all. The words moved to the help's **Row Icons**
legend, where a sentence has room to be right — which is the whole reason
`nodeTypeLabel` survives the column that used to be its only caller. The rough
edge is still there, in the legend; it is simply not repeated on every row.

Cost: **+0.55 MB** on the binary (24.4 → 25.0).

Worth knowing: **go-gitlab retries 5xx** with an exponential backoff — a test
serving 500 took 35 seconds, measured. Not a regression (it is the SDK's
default), but an unreachable instance makes the user wait behind a spinner.

## The vocabulary — `forge.Vocabulary`

What a forge is **called**, as opposed to what it can do. The distinction is
§3.6's and it is the whole design: "Group" against "Organization" is a *word*,
while nesting depth and the visibility set are *shapes* — they change what the
application can promise, and no wording helps with them. `Shape` carries the
second, `Vocabulary` the first, and neither grows conditionals for the other.

**Per forge, not neutral.** A GitLab user says *group*, a GitHub user says
*repository*; "namespace" is a third language nobody speaks and makes the
application read as an abstraction layer rather than as a tool. The *field
names* are neutral because the code has to be — a view cannot switch on which
forge it is talking to — but nothing a user reads is.

**Resolved from the config, not from the session.** `forge.VocabularyFor(
cfg.Forge.Type)`, not a method on `Forge` and not a field on `shared.State`:
the explorer's "not authenticated" screen and the auth view's own title both
need the words *before* any session exists, so a value hanging off a live
backend would be missing exactly where it is needed most. Each view has a small
`vocab()` helper; the config is what every one of them already holds.

**No view writes anything specific to one forge into a string, and a test says
so.** `internal/ui/vocabtest` parses every `.go` under `internal/ui` and fails
on a string literal containing a forge **marker** — import paths excluded, and
one declared exception (`theme.ForgeIcon`'s own switch), on the model of
`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`. A wording table nothing enforces drifts back one
message at a time, and the messages that drift are the ones nobody reads until a
GitHub context renders "GitLab not authenticated".

The markers are the two **names** *and* the token **prefixes** (`glpat-`,
`ghp_`, `github_pat_`, …), and the second half was added after the first half
missed something. The auth view carried `glpat-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx` as its
token placeholder for the whole of §3.6, and this test walked past it every
time: a token prefix is forge-specific **without naming a forge**, which is
exactly the shape a guard on names cannot see. `Vocabulary.TokenPlaceholder`
carries it now — shaped like a real value, because that is what a placeholder
is, while the prose about which prefixes exist lives in `TokenHelp`, where there
is room to name more than one.

**A command name is not vocabulary.** It is routing identity, the same for both
forges (§3.6 step 8 makes it `git-auth`), so a message quoting one builds it
from `command.ViewGitlabAuth` rather than writing it out. That is also what
makes the message survive the rename instead of quietly outliving it.

**The icon is the theme's, keyed on the same constant.** `theme.ForgeIcon` and
`forge.VocabularyFor` are two tables because a domain package must not import
the UI — but both switch on `config.ForgeGitLab` / `config.ForgeGitHub` rather
than on a literal, so there is one spelling of "gitlab" in the application and a
new forge cannot be half-added.

What is *not* in the vocabulary, and deliberately: the visibility set (a shape,
on `Shape`), the humanised role (the backend's, because GitLab's numbers and
GitHub's words do not align), and the token prefix as a *check* — it is a hint,
`TokenPlaceholder`, and DevDesk validates nothing, so saying "must" about it is
how a user comes to believe a working token is broken.

Sites it took over: the explorer's title, its loading line, its empty and
signed-out screens, its Type column and its help; the auth view's title, help,
URL label and both "not configured" messages; the dashboard's Code box, its
tree root and its help; the configuration view's forge tab — its title, its
icon, its URL example and two field labels; and `CreationForm`'s two resource
types.


## The CI status vocabulary (D66)

`Repository.CIStatus` is a **closed set of words, and it is GitLab's**:
`created`, `waiting_for_resource`, `preparing`, `pending`, `running`,
`success`, `failed`, `canceled`, `skipped`, `manual`, `scheduled`. They are
declared in `internal/forge/cistatus.go` and listed by `CIStatuses()`.

The choice is historical rather than principled — GitLab was the only backend
when the field was added, so its own word went straight into the explorer's CI
column. Keeping it is still right: eleven values against GitHub's nine, and it
separates "queued" from "not started", so translating GitHub onto it loses less
than the reverse would.

**A promise that only a comment made was not kept.** `lastWorkflowConclusion`
claimed to return "the same words the GitLab backend reports" and returned
GitHub's: of the nine outcomes Actions can produce, only `success` and `skipped`
happen to be spelled the same. `failure`, `cancelled` and `in_progress` reached
the CI column as raw text truncated to its six cells — `failu…`, `cance…`,
`in_pr…` — and, worse, coloured by `pipelineStatusStyle`'s default branch, which
is the **warning** style. A broken build read as a caution, in the one column
that exists to make a broken build obvious.

Four GitHub outcomes have no counterpart and are folded rather than dropped,
each on its own argument:

| GitHub | becomes | why |
|---|---|---|
| `timed_out`, `startup_failure` | `failed` | GitLab kills a timed-out job as `failed`; folding reports what GitLab would have |
| `action_required` | `manual` | a run waiting for an approval is exactly what GitLab calls manual |
| `neutral`, `stale` | `skipped` | GitHub renders both the way it renders skipped, and skipped is the only grey this set has |
| `queued`, `requested`, `waiting`, `pending` | `pending` | GitLab's four pre-run states differ to a scheduler, not to a reader |

**An unrecognised value becomes the empty string, never itself.** That is what
`Repository.CIStatus` documents for a value a backend has no equivalent for, and
it is the difference between an empty cell and six characters of a platform's
internal spelling.

**Two tests hold the contract, and neither existed before.**
`TestTheBackendOnlyEmitsDeclaredStatuses` walks the GitHub mapping tables and
refuses an output `CIStatuses()` does not declare;
`TestEveryDeclaredCIStatusHasAnIcon` walks the same list from the view and
refuses a status `pipelineStatusLabel` has no glyph for. The second is what
found the GitLab half of the defect: `created` and `scheduled` were missing from
that switch and printed their own names too.

The view's `default:` branch survives both. It is unreachable for a backend that
keeps the promise, and it is what a backend that breaks it should hit — a
truncated word is a bad answer, and no answer at all is worse.
## The explorer table (§3.56)

Eight columns, in this order: **icon, Name, Slug, Visibility, Role, CI, Created,
Activity**. Two of them are glyphs.

The **first** carries the node kind and follows Rule 125 — untitled, two cells,
no comparator, no search key. It replaced a thirteen-cell `Type` column printing
"Group" or "Organization", and the eleven cells it returns go to Name and Slug,
the two columns that identify a row.

**Visibility** is a glyph under its own whole word: a globe for public, a shield
for internal, a lock for private, and an **empty cell** for anything else — a
forge that grows a fourth value must not be shown one of the three that exist.
The word stays because it is what makes the three decodable without a legend,
and it costs nothing: the column is exactly ten cells, the width of its own
header. That is affordable only because the column **stopped sorting** — every
sortable column reserves two cells for an arrow, sorted or not
(`datatable/widths.go:askFor`), and three visibilities in an order nobody would
agree on were never a sort worth the width.

The glyphs are deliberately none of the workspaces set. `ws` lists what is on
disk and `exp` lists what the forge holds; a row that looked the same in both
would claim they are the same object.

**The table opens unsorted** (`SortColumn: -1`), which is not a change of
behaviour: `loadChildren` stacks namespaces then repositories, and the sort by
node type it replaced is the identity on that list. What is gained is that `.`
now has "no sort" as a stop, so the forge's own order is reachable again after
cycling away from it — a sort by type could never express that.

## Creating and deleting — the row is the progress

`N` and `D` are network calls, and the tree used to answer neither of them while
one was in flight. A create ran `handleRefresh()` on the way out: the table was
emptied and re-listed from scratch, so for the whole of the round trip the user
saw a blank body and a footer with nothing in it — and then the thing they had
asked for, with no thread connecting the two.

**The row goes on screen when the request goes out.** `insertCreatingNode` puts
a `TreeNode{Creating: true}` at the level being browsed, keyed on the path
predicted from the parent and the slug; the spinner rides in the icon column
(`iconCell`), where the kind glyph will be. When the forge answers,
`settleCreating` swaps the placeholder for the real node **in place** — no
refresh, because the forge has just said what it made and re-listing the tree to
learn it would empty the table a second time. A failure takes the row away again
and says so in the footer.

Three things follow, and each is the reason for a piece of the shape:

| | |
|---|---|
| The path is a **prediction** | the row needs a key before there is an answer. The forge is free to differ, so `Target` travels on the message — it is the only thing that can still find the row that was put on screen |
| The spinner comes from the **broadcast** | this view's own chain stops on `!m.loading` (`handleSpinnerTick`), so a frame taken from it would freeze on frame zero the moment the tree settled. It is D5's argument, reached from the other side |
| The row is **inert** while it spins | `actionable()` refuses it, `GetShortcuts` greys `D`, and pressing the key says which of the two reasons applies (Rule 130). A placeholder carries no identifier, so an action addressing one would send an empty ID |

Both are `jobs` runs (`KindCreate`, `KindDelete`) rather than a local flag — see
the jobs registry in [`app-shell.md`](app-shell.md) for why a single-item run
still earns one. The delete keeps its row and takes the same spinner: a row that
vanished before the answer came would be claiming something that has not
happened yet.

## The explorer clone

`C` in the explorer opens a **selection mode** over the same tree, and `enter`
starts a **pipeline** that discovers and clones at once (§3.16). It replaced a
single `Cmd` covering a whole subtree behind a modal reading `"Pulling..."` —
several minutes indistinguishable from a freeze on a large group.

The line that holds it together: **the explorer creates what does not exist,
workspaces reconciles what does.** A repository already on disk is skipped
untouched, so the explorer never needs to know what a dirty working tree is and
the per-row states collapse to five — queued, cloning, cloned, already there,
failed. Updating an existing clone is §3.17's `sync`, in workspaces.

Those five states are where `jobs.ItemState` came from, and since §3.58 they
*are* it: this screen is the item level of a clone run (D3), rendering a record
the router owns rather than keeping one of its own.

| Mode | Screen | Keys |
|---|---|---|
| `ModeSelecting` | the tree, with a checkbox in the icon column | `space` ticks, `←→` drill, `enter` confirms, `esc` cancels |
| `ModeCloning` | a flat list, one row per repository | `esc` cancels, then closes |

**The selection is roots plus exclusions, never a list of repositories**
(`selection.go`). A positive list cannot be built when a group is ticked without
enumerating its children — the full API walk, run at selection time, which is
the freeze moved one screen earlier. "This group, minus these" needs to know
nothing about what the group contains, so a group nobody has expanded can still
be ticked, displayed with the right tri-state, and walked. It is the only
representation compatible with discovering as you clone.

The **nodes** are kept separately, in `Model.selectionNodes`: the walk has to
start from one, and a root ticked three levels down is no longer on screen once
the user has come back up. The selection itself stays paths-only, which is what
lets it answer for paths nobody has fetched.

**The check state travels on a row type.** `datatable` columns are built once in
`New` and close over nothing, so the table moved from `Model[*TreeNode]` to
`Model[explorerRow]` (`row.go`) — the `imageRow` pattern. The state must **not**
move into `datatable`: `SetItems` replaces the items on every drill-down, while
the selection spans levels the table has never shown. `RenderCheckboxTri` styles
its output and so cannot go in a cell; `checkboxIcon` is the glyph without it
(Rule 122).

The checkbox **rides on the icon cell** rather than taking a column of its own.
A column would cost four cells on every screen to say nothing on all but one of
them, and at 80 columns the explorer has none to spare.

Since §3.56 that cell is two wide (Rule 125), so the checkbox and the kind glyph
cannot sit side by side — the box replaces the glyph. **What keeps the sharing
honest is the colour**: `iconStyle` paints `theme.IconRoleNamespace` or
`theme.IconRoleRepository` in both modes, so a ticked row still says group or
repository by hue. That is the one thing the icon-colour roles were added for,
and it is why they are not decoration.

### The clone is a run of the registry (§3.58, D3)

`cloneList` used to hold five states, a slice of rows, an index keyed on the
path and a spinner frame of its own. That was the fifth bookkeeping beside the
four `internal/jobs` replaced — and the one the plan named as the prototype to
generalise, because it was already a jobs view for a single kind.

It renders the run now, and owns none of it:

| | |
|---|---|
| the rows | `jobs.Run.Items`, from the snapshot the router broadcasts |
| the frame | the router's one chain (D5), taken bare — a table cell is measured before it is styled (Rule 122) |
| "finished" | `Run.Finished()`, not a flag this screen sets |
| the mapping | `CloneEventMsg.Transition()` — the clone's own vocabulary, in the clone's package, which is what `jobs.Reporter` exists for |

**A clone run is *open***, and it is the only kind that is. Every other launch
site knows its full target list when it dispatches, which is what makes "8
waiting" sayable (D10); the clone's walk *is* what finds them, so
`jobs.NewOpenRun` registers a run with none and `Registry.Discover` adds each as
the walk turns it up. An open run is **never finished** whatever its items say —
a walk that has found three repositories and cloned all three is still going,
and settling it there would stop the spinner and print a summary the next
repository contradicts. `CloneRunFinishedMsg` seals it, through `jobs.Sealer`: a
second interface because a closed channel names no target.

What this buys is the thing D3 asked for: **`:jobs` shows the same clone the
explorer is rendering**, without either copy being authoritative and without the
explorer having to be on screen for its rows to keep moving.

**Two cancellation scopes, and the distinction is the point** (`pipeline.go`).
`cloneRun.cancel` is a `context.CancelFunc` covering **discovery only** — HTTP
reads, which cancel safely. A `git clone` is never interrupted: a context that
kills one leaves half a repository on disk, which is exactly what this avoids.
So `esc` cancels the walk and the scheduler stops issuing work, the running
clones are awaited, and the footer says `Cancelling — 3 clones finishing`. A
second `esc` must not force.

`esc` goes **through the registry** (`jobs.CancelOpenMsg`), which holds the
cancel function from the launch. Calling the pipeline's own would stop the walk
behind the record's back and leave `:jobs` claiming the run finished on its
own — the distinction `Run.cancelled` exists to keep. Cancelling also seals:
the walk that would have closed the run is precisely what was stopped, so
leaving it open would keep it unsettled for the life of the session.

The message names a **kind**, not an identifier. A progressive run belongs to a
screen that owns the display while it goes, so there is one open clone at a
time and the view can name it without holding a `JobID` — the registry state D1
keeps out of views.

`cloneWalkFailed` is a kind of its own: a group that cannot be listed gets a
failed row naming the **group**, because the repositories under it were never
discovered and no other row can stand for them.

The **failures are named when the run ends**, in the footer and the log. The
list is discarded on `esc` and workspaces records only the successes — a clone
that failed wrote nothing, so that report is the only one there will be.

`gitlab.pull.include_archived` is read by `listGroupChildren` and **only by the
clone**: browsing lists everything the forge has.

**A clone may never prompt, and `gitlab.Clone` is where that is enforced.**
Sending git's streams to the null device does not prevent a credential prompt —
it prevents git asking *itself*, after which the **credential helper** takes
over, and a helper is a separate process. Git Credential Manager writes
`info: please complete authentication in your browser` to the console directly,
over the top of the rendered frame, then waits. Bubble Tea cannot recover a
frame something else has written into: two frames end up visible at once, and
the row spins with nothing on screen saying why. Observed, not theorised.

So `cloneEnv` shuts every interactive path — `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`,
`GCM_INTERACTIVE=never`, both askpass hooks, ssh in `BatchMode` — and the token
DevDesk already holds is passed as `http.extraHeader` **through the
environment**: argv is readable from the process list, and the `user:token@host`
URL form is written into every cloned repository's `.git/config` and stays
there. A stalled transfer is bounded by `http.lowSpeedLimit`/`lowSpeedTime`
rather than by killing the process, so git cleans up after itself and decision
12 still holds.

The consequence to keep in mind: with the helper out of the loop, a context
whose stored token is missing or under-scoped **fails** rather than falling back
to a browser. That is the intended trade — a failed row naming git's reason
beats a spinner that never resolves — but it makes the token the only way in.

1	# Configuration — the schema and the view
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	## Configuration System
7	
8	Config loaded from `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` with schema defined in `internal/config/config.go`:
9	- `App` - Global settings (theme, default view, workspaces dir, `show_hidden_files`, `secret_backend`)
10	- `Status` - Monitoring settings (refresh interval, components)
11	- `Forge` - the platform this context targets: `type`, URL and clone settings
12	- `Registry` - OCI registry configuration (see Registry model below)
13	- `Scan` - Security scanning (Trivy, Gitleaks)
14	- `Network` - what the netdiag view runs on: the tool image, and the dials
15	  `internal/netcheck` used to hardcode
16	- `MCP` - the read-only MCP server (§3.38): `enabled`, off by default, and
17	  `expose`, an allow-list of tool names
18	
19	**`forge:` was `gitlab:`, and the rename is migrated rather than announced.**
20	A context targets one platform (§3.6), so the section is named after the role
21	rather than after the one implementation there was, and it gains a `type:` —
22	`gitlab` or `github`, **declared, never sniffed**, on the registry `provider`
23	precedent. An absent `type` means `gitlab`, which is what every file written
24	before the key existed meant.
25	
26	`migrateGitLabSection` runs **first** in `applyDefaults`, and that ordering is
27	the whole of it. Every default below writes into `cfg.Forge`, so a migration
28	placed after them finds a block that is no longer empty, takes the
29	field-by-field path, and silently drops the user's own `parallel_jobs: 7` — that
30	is not a hazard imagined for the comment, it is what the first draft did and
31	what `TestAConfigCarryingRetiredKeysStillLoads` caught. The other half of the
32	reason is `docker:` → `network:`'s: `yaml.Unmarshal` is not strict here, so an
33	un-migrated block is dropped in silence, and the silence would point a context
34	at no host at all.
35	
36	**A whole-block copy when `forge:` is absent, field by field when both are
37	present.** The distinction exists for one field: `IncludeArchived` is a bool, so
38	"unset" and "deliberately false" are the same value and no per-field guard can
39	tell them apart — it can only be carried over when the new block says nothing at
40	all. When both are present the new one wins field by field: its values were
41	written later, and overwriting them with the old ones would undo the edit that
42	created the situation.
43	
44	`forge.type` is stated in `internal/config` and in each backend's `Shape()`, and
45	`TestTheForgeVocabularyMatchesTheConfig` holds the two in step — config must not
46	import a backend, and a backend must not be the authority on what a config file
47	may say, so a test is the only thing that can. Same arrangement as the registry
48	`provider` names.
49	
50	The legacy secret migration is unaffected and the order is worth knowing:
51	`credentials.MigrateLegacySecrets` reads the **raw file** at router
52	construction, before anything can save, so a plaintext `gitlab.token` reaches
53	the store before the rename can rewrite the file without it.
54	
55	**`network:` was `docker:`.** The one key `docker:` held was never a Docker
56	setting, and the four other tabs of the configuration view are each named
57	after the section they write. That key — the image the OCI connectivity test
58	ran — has since been removed along with the feature itself; `NetworkConfig`
59	now holds only the netdiag dials (`CheckTimeout`, `PingCount`,
60	`CertExpiryWarnDays`, `PortsRefreshInterval`).
61	
62	**`app.container_engine`** names the engine every container, image, network and
63	volume comes from: `auto` (the default — docker if it is on PATH, else podman),
64	`docker`, `podman`, or an explicit path to a binary. It sits in `app` beside
65	`ide_command` and `terminal_command` — the section that already holds the
66	external tools this application drives — and deliberately **not** in `network:`,
67	which carries only netcheck's dials despite its old name (§3.67).
68	
69	`auto` is written on load rather than left empty, for the same reason
70	`secret_backend` is: `engine.Resolve` reads `""` as auto either way, but the
71	configuration view cycles a closed set and a value outside it has nowhere to
72	start from. The names are stated in `internal/config` and in `internal/engine`,
73	held in step by `TestEveryConfiguredEngineHasAShape` — the same arrangement as
74	`forge.type`, one paragraph up. The field settles **on blur**, like the forge:
75	cycling auto → docker → podman would otherwise re-resolve three times.
76	`ConfigSavedMsg.EngineChanged` is what tells the router, because rebuilding the
77	views is not enough on its own — they would be rebuilt against the engine that
78	is still resolved.
79	
80	**No secret goes in this file.** `GitLabConfig` has no `Token` and
81	`RegistryConfig` has no `Password`; both live in the host secret store (see
82	Credentials Management). Do not add a secret-bearing field back — the schema is
83	what makes the guarantee checkable.
84	
85	Config is injected into views at creation. Use `config.Save()` to persist changes.
86	
87	## Configuration view — `internal/ui/configuration`
88	
89	Edits every **scalar** setting a context carries, in six tabs (`app`, the
90	forge's own name, `scan`, `network`, `mcp`, `status`). The second is titled after the
91	platform the context targets — `gitlab` or `github` — rather than after the
92	section key: `forge:` is what the file says, and no user calls it that. Lists stay where they are consulted: monitors keep
93	their CRUD in `status`, registries keep `RegistryForm` in `oci-resources`.
94	Duplicating them here would be the opposite of the point.
95	
96	Tabs are not decoration. Rule 135 reserves `Tab` for tabs and `↑↓` for fields,
97	so a tabbed form is the only layout where both keys have exactly one job.
98	
99	Settings are declared as a table of `field` values in `fields.go`, each holding
100	**one pointer accessor** into the config (`func(*config.Config) *string`) rather
101	than a get/set pair. Twenty-nine settings with two closures each is where the
102	copy-paste defects of §2 came from; one reference means the read and the write
103	cannot disagree about which setting they mean.
104	`TestEveryFieldCarriesTheAccessorItsKindNeeds` and
105	`TestNoTwoFieldsAddressTheSameSetting` are what keep the table honest.
106	
107	Fields inside a tab are grouped under a heading with a Nerd Font icon
108	(`SubTitleStyle`, the same treatment the security form used): `scan` separates
109	**Scanners**, **Trivy**, **Gitleaks**, **Plumber** and **Limits**. `group()` stamps the
110	heading onto a contiguous run rather than each field carrying its own, so a run
111	cannot be split by a typo and render its heading twice —
112	`TestEachTabRendersItsGroupHeadingsOnceInOrder` pins that.
113	
114	**The header names the context, and the title does not.** A configuration
115	belongs to one, and editing `workspaces_dir` in the wrong context is otherwise
116	silent because the fields look identical in all of them — but that is what
117	`GetHeaderInfo` says here as it does in every other view, so a title repeating
118	it was the same fact twice on one screen. `GetTitle()` is `󰙨 Configuration`.
119	
120	**The context's file path is a row in the form, not a header field.** It sits in
121	**Paths** under `workspaces_dir`, because that is what it belongs beside; the
122	header is for what changes as the user moves, and the file does not. It is the
123	one `kindStatic` field — shown, never written, and `Model.settleFocus` walks the
124	cursor past it in whichever direction it was already moving, since a focus
125	indicator on a row no key acts upon says the opposite of what is true. The
126	**Paths** group therefore reads three paths and then the checkbox that qualifies
127	them (`show_hidden_files`): a checkbox wedged between two value rows breaks the
128	column they share.
129	
130	Chevrons and values are aligned on one column per tab, padded on the **head**
131	(label plus a cycle field's select icon) rather than on the label — padding the
132	label leaves a cycle field's chevron two cells right of every other. Checkboxes
133	are excluded from the measurement: they have no value, so a long checkbox label
134	would push every value right for nothing. `theme.RenderCheckbox` already emits
135	the focus indicator, so the view must not add a second.
136	
137	| Kind | Control | Persists |
138	|---|---|---|
139	| closed set | cycle `←→` (Rule 132) | immediately |
140	| boolean | checkbox, `Space` only | immediately |
141	| text / integer | `textinput` | on blur, **after validation** |
142	
143	**A refused value keeps the cursor on its field.** An unparseable integer or a
144	malformed Trivy address is reported (Rule 128) and *not* written — coercing to
145	zero is how `trivy_server: ":"` reached a config file in the first place.
146
