# Configuration — the schema and the view

> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
> read this file when working on the code it describes.

## Configuration System

Config loaded from `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` with schema defined in `internal/config/config.go`:
- `App` - Global settings (theme, default view, workspaces dir, `show_hidden_files`, `secret_backend`)
- `Status` - Monitoring settings (refresh interval, components)
- `Forge` - the platform this context targets: `type`, URL and clone settings
- `Registry` - OCI registry configuration (see Registry model below)
- `Scan` - Security scanning (Trivy, Gitleaks)
- `Network` - what the netdiag view runs on: the tool image, and the dials
  `internal/netcheck` used to hardcode
- `MCP` - the read-only MCP server (§3.38): `enabled`, off by default, and
  `expose`, an allow-list of tool names

**`forge:` was `gitlab:`, and the rename is migrated rather than announced.**
A context targets one platform (§3.6), so the section is named after the role
rather than after the one implementation there was, and it gains a `type:` —
`gitlab` or `github`, **declared, never sniffed**, on the registry `provider`
precedent. An absent `type` means `gitlab`, which is what every file written
before the key existed meant.

`migrateGitLabSection` runs **first** in `applyDefaults`, and that ordering is
the whole of it. Every default below writes into `cfg.Forge`, so a migration
placed after them finds a block that is no longer empty, takes the
field-by-field path, and silently drops the user's own `parallel_jobs: 7` — that
is not a hazard imagined for the comment, it is what the first draft did and
what `TestAConfigCarryingRetiredKeysStillLoads` caught. The other half of the
reason is `docker:` → `network:`'s: `yaml.Unmarshal` is not strict here, so an
un-migrated block is dropped in silence, and the silence would point a context
at no host at all.

**A whole-block copy when `forge:` is absent, field by field when both are
present.** The distinction exists for one field: `IncludeArchived` is a bool, so
"unset" and "deliberately false" are the same value and no per-field guard can
tell them apart — it can only be carried over when the new block says nothing at
all. When both are present the new one wins field by field: its values were
written later, and overwriting them with the old ones would undo the edit that
created the situation.

`forge.type` is stated in `internal/config` and in each backend's `Shape()`, and
`TestTheForgeVocabularyMatchesTheConfig` holds the two in step — config must not
import a backend, and a backend must not be the authority on what a config file
may say, so a test is the only thing that can. Same arrangement as the registry
`provider` names.

The legacy secret migration is unaffected and the order is worth knowing:
`credentials.MigrateLegacySecrets` reads the **raw file** at router
construction, before anything can save, so a plaintext `gitlab.token` reaches
the store before the rename can rewrite the file without it.

**`network:` was `docker:`.** The one key `docker:` held was never a Docker
setting, and the four other tabs of the configuration view are each named
after the section they write. That key — the image the OCI connectivity test
ran — has since been removed along with the feature itself; `NetworkConfig`
now holds only the netdiag dials (`CheckTimeout`, `PingCount`,
`CertExpiryWarnDays`, `PortsRefreshInterval`).

**`app.container_engine`** names the engine every container, image, network and
volume comes from: `auto` (the default — docker if it is on PATH, else podman),
`docker`, `podman`, or an explicit path to a binary. It sits in `app` beside
`ide_command` and `terminal_command` — the section that already holds the
external tools this application drives — and deliberately **not** in `network:`,
which carries only netcheck's dials despite its old name (§3.67).

`auto` is written on load rather than left empty, for the same reason
`secret_backend` is: `engine.Resolve` reads `""` as auto either way, but the
configuration view cycles a closed set and a value outside it has nowhere to
start from. The names are stated in `internal/config` and in `internal/engine`,
held in step by `TestEveryConfiguredEngineHasAShape` — the same arrangement as
`forge.type`, one paragraph up. The field settles **on blur**, like the forge:
cycling auto → docker → podman would otherwise re-resolve three times.
`ConfigSavedMsg.EngineChanged` is what tells the router, because rebuilding the
views is not enough on its own — they would be rebuilt against the engine that
is still resolved.

**No secret goes in this file.** `GitLabConfig` has no `Token` and
`RegistryConfig` has no `Password`; both live in the host secret store (see
Credentials Management). Do not add a secret-bearing field back — the schema is
what makes the guarantee checkable.

Config is injected into views at creation. Use `config.Save()` to persist changes.

## Configuration view — `internal/ui/configuration`

Edits every **scalar** setting a context carries, in six tabs (`app`, the
forge's own name, `scan`, `network`, `mcp`, `status`). The second is titled after the
platform the context targets — `gitlab` or `github` — rather than after the
section key: `forge:` is what the file says, and no user calls it that. Lists stay where they are consulted: monitors keep
their CRUD in `status`, registries keep `RegistryForm` in `oci-resources`.
Duplicating them here would be the opposite of the point.

Tabs are not decoration. Rule 135 reserves `Tab` for tabs and `↑↓` for fields,
so a tabbed form is the only layout where both keys have exactly one job.

Settings are declared as a table of `field` values in `fields.go`, each holding
**one pointer accessor** into the config (`func(*config.Config) *string`) rather
than a get/set pair. Twenty-nine settings with two closures each is where the
copy-paste defects of §2 came from; one reference means the read and the write
cannot disagree about which setting they mean.
`TestEveryFieldCarriesTheAccessorItsKindNeeds` and
`TestNoTwoFieldsAddressTheSameSetting` are what keep the table honest.

Fields inside a tab are grouped under a heading with a Nerd Font icon
(`SubTitleStyle`, the same treatment the security form used): `scan` separates
**Scanners**, **Trivy**, **Gitleaks**, **Plumber** and **Limits**. `group()` stamps the
heading onto a contiguous run rather than each field carrying its own, so a run
cannot be split by a typo and render its heading twice —
`TestEachTabRendersItsGroupHeadingsOnceInOrder` pins that.

**The header names the context, and the title does not.** A configuration
belongs to one, and editing `workspaces_dir` in the wrong context is otherwise
silent because the fields look identical in all of them — but that is what
`GetHeaderInfo` says here as it does in every other view, so a title repeating
it was the same fact twice on one screen. `GetTitle()` is `󰙨 Configuration`.

**The context's file path is a row in the form, not a header field.** It sits in

header is for what changes as the user moves, and the file does not. It is the

cursor past it in whichever direction it was already moving, since a focus

column they share.

Chevrons and values are aligned on one column per tab, padded on the **head**

are excluded from the measurement: they have no value, so a long checkbox label
would push every value right for nothing. `theme.RenderCheckbox` already emits
the focus indicator, so the view must not add a second.

|---|---|---|
| closed set | cycle `←→` (Rule 132) | immediately |
| boolean | checkbox, `Space` only | immediately |
| text / integer | `textinput` | on blur, **after validation** |

I now have a complete picture. Here is the concise report.

## 1. `Config` struct schema — `internal/config/config.go`

```go
type Config struct {                                    // config.go:14
    App      AppConfig      `yaml:"app"`
    Status   StatusConfig   `yaml:"status"`
    Forge    ForgeConfig    `yaml:"forge"`
    Registry RegistryConfig `yaml:"registry"`
    Scan     ScanConfig     `yaml:"scan"`
    Network  NetworkConfig  `yaml:"network"`
    MCP      MCPConfig      `yaml:"mcp"`
    GitLab   GitLabConfig   `yaml:"gitlab,omitempty"` // Deprecated: use Forge
}
```

- `AppConfig` (config.go:135): `Theme`, `LogFile`, `DefaultView`, `WorkspacesDir`, `IDECommand`, `TerminalCommand`, `TerminalNewWindow`, `ShowHiddenFiles`, `SecretBackend`, `ContainerEngine`.
- `ForgeConfig` (config.go:184): `Type` (`gitlab`/`github`), `URL`, `DefaultParentGroup`, `DefaultVisibility`, `CloneMethod`, `Pull ForgePullConfig{ParallelJobs, IncludeArchived}`. No token field — token lives in the secret store (`internal/credentials`).
- `GitLabConfig`/`GitLabPullConfig` (config.go:210,221) — deprecated shadow of the above, migrated at load then cleared.
- `RegistryConfig` (config.go:280): `URL`, `Username`, `TemplatesRepository`, `CacheDir`, `Registries []RegistryItem`.
- `RegistryItem` (config.go:228): `Slug`, `Kind` (`registry`/`group`), `Parent`, `Provider`, `URL`, `Username`, `Alias`, `RepoPrefix`, `AuthMode` (`credentials`/`anonymous`/`inherit`), `AuthEnabled` (deprecated), `ManagementURL`.
- `ScanConfig` (config.go:305): per-tool `*Source`/`*Path`/`*Image` triples for Trivy/Gitleaks/Plumber, `UseTrivyServer`/`TrivyServer`, `CacheDir`, `MaxCachedReports`, `Timeout`, `MaxConcurrentScans`, plus scan-option bools `EnableVuln/EnableSecret/EnableMisconfig/EnableLicense/IgnoreUnfixed/IgnoreEOL/GitleaksHistory/GitleaksConfig/EnableCIScore/PlumberConfig`.
- `StatusConfig`/`ComponentConfig` (config.go:349,357): monitoring, `Type` is `http/https/icmp/dns`.
- `NetworkConfig` (config.go:100): `CheckTimeout`, `PingCount`, `CertExpiryWarnDays`, `PortsRefreshInterval`.
- `MCPConfig` (config.go:61): `Enabled`, `Expose []string`, `Listen` (default `127.0.0.1:7777`, const `DefaultMCPListen`, config.go:97).

**Closed-value-set helpers** (mirrors of what the config view cycles through):
- `ContainerEngines() []string` — `internal/config/engine.go:24` → `{EngineAuto, EngineDocker, EnginePodman}` (consts at engine.go:9-15).
- `ForgeTypes() []string` — `internal/config/forge.go:18` → `{ForgeGitLab, ForgeGitHub}` (consts at forge.go:9-14).
- `Providers() []string` — `internal/config/registries.go:82` → generic/nexus/harbor/artifactory/gitlab (consts at registries.go:20-25).
- `Kinds() []string` — registries.go:87 (`registry`/`group`).
- `AuthModes(isMember bool) []string` — registries.go:47 → `{inherit, anonymous}` for a group member, else `{credentials, anonymous}` (consts registries.go:36-38: `AuthCredentials`, `AuthAnonymous`, `AuthInherit`).
- `ToolSourceAuto/Binary/Image` consts — config.go:295-301 (scan tool source, closed set `auto|binary|image`).
- `theme.ListThemes() ([]string, error)` — `internal/ui/theme/manager.go:181` (always includes `"default"` plus JSON files in `~/.devdesk/themes`); `theme.LoadTheme(name)` at manager.go:150 also accepts legacy `""`/`"dark"` as aliases for `"default"`.
- `credentials.Select(contextName, preference string) Selection` — `internal/credentials/select.go:76`; preference consts `PreferenceAuto/PreferenceKeyring/PreferenceGitCredential` (select.go:31-34); backend consts `BackendKeyring/BackendGitCredential/BackendMemory` (select.go:17-26). `app.secret_backend` accepts `auto|keyring|git-credential` (no explicit "list" helper — the view apparently just hardcodes/cycles these two-plus-auto names; check `internal/ui/configuration/fields.go` if you need the exact cycling literal).

## 2. On-disk context storage — all in `internal/config/config.go`

- Directory: `ConfigDir()` (config.go:594) → `~/.devdesk`. `EnsureConfigDir()` (config.go:603) does `os.MkdirAll(dir, 0755)`.
- Current context pointer: `~/.devdesk/.current-context`, a plain-text file holding the context name, read by `GetCurrentContext()` (config.go:627), written by `SetCurrentContext(name)` (config.go:669, validates name, writes `0600`). `CurrentContextName()` (config.go:660) is the panic-free helper wrapper.
- File naming: `GetContextPath(contextName)` (config.go:860) → `"default"` → `~/.devdesk/config.yaml`; anything else → `~/.devdesk/config-<name>.yaml`.
- Name validation: `ValidateContextName(name)` (config.go:880) — `"default"` or regex `^[a-z0-9-]+$`.
- Listing: `ListContexts() ([]string, error)` (config.go:692) — includes `"default"` if `config.yaml` exists, plus a glob over `config-*.yaml`.
- Existence check: `ContextExists(contextName) (bool, error)` (config.go:836).
- Load/save a specific context: `LoadContext(contextName) (*Config, error)` (config.go:728) — reads YAML, unmarshals, calls `applyDefaults`, then `ExpandPaths`; errors if the file is missing. `SaveContext(cfg, contextName) error` (config.go:810) — validates name, ensures dir, marshals with `yaml.Marshal`, writes `0600`.
- Convenience wrappers around the current context: `Load() (*Config, error)` (config.go:374, falls back to `Default()` if the file doesn't exist) and `Save(cfg) error` (config.go:613).
- **`CreateContext(contextName) error`** (config.go:900) is the closest existing analogue to what `dk setup` needs: validates the name, refuses if it already exists (`ContextExists`), builds `cfg := Default()`, clears `cfg.Status.Components` and `cfg.Forge.URL`, then `SaveContext(cfg, contextName)`. A setup wizard would likely want to call `Default()`, populate fields interactively, then either reuse `CreateContext`'s "must not exist" semantics or call `SaveContext` directly for an explicit overwrite path (note `CreateContext` itself has no overwrite option — it errors when the context exists, so an "overwrite" wizard flag would need new logic, e.g. checking `ContextExists` itself and skipping that guard, or a new `OverwriteContext`-style function).

## 3. `applyDefaults` — config.go:397-534

Order matters (comment at config.go:400 explains why migration runs first). It:
1. `migrateGitLabSection(cfg)` — `gitlab:` → `forge:` (forge.go:32).
2. Normalizes `App.Theme`: `""` or `"dark"` → `"default"`.
3. Fills empty-string/zero defaults for: `LogFile` (`~/.devdesk/devdesk.log`), `DefaultView` (`"dashboard"`), `WorkspacesDir` (`~/workspaces`), `IDECommand` (`"code"`), `SecretBackend` (`"auto"`), `ContainerEngine` (`EngineAuto`), `Status.RefreshInterval` (10), `Status.Timeout` (5), `Forge.Type` (`ForgeGitLab`), `Forge.DefaultVisibility` (`"private"`), `Forge.CloneMethod` (`"https"`), `Forge.Pull.ParallelJobs` (4), `Registry.CacheDir` (`~/.devdesk/cache/templates`).
4. Migrates a legacy single-registry (`Registry.URL`/`Username`) into `Registry.Registries` with `AuthMode: AuthCredentials`.
5. `Scan.CacheDir` (`~/.devdesk/cache/scans`), `MaxCachedReports` (50), `Timeout` (300), `MaxConcurrentScans` (3), `MCP.Listen` (`DefaultMCPListen`), the three `*Source` fields → `ToolSourceAuto`.
6. `Network.*` fields default to the `Default*` consts (8, 3, 30, 2).
7. "All scan-option bools false" → treated as "never configured", sets `EnableVuln`/`EnableSecret` true (deliberately excludes `EnableCIScore` from that check — see comment at config.go:519).
8. Last: `normalizeRegistries(cfg.Registry.Registries)` — can return an error (duplicate slug, missing parent group), which is the *only* error path out of `applyDefaults`.

`Default() *Config` (config.go:537) is the from-scratch equivalent, hardcoding the same values without any migration, for a wizard to start from.

## 4. CLI/main.go dispatch

`main.go` has **no subcommand system at all** — no `flag`, no `cobra`, no `os.Args` parsing anywhere in the repo (verified with a repo-wide grep, zero hits outside this file's own comment). `main()` (main.go:32) calls `runTUI()` unconditionally; the comment at main.go:22-31 explicitly notes that a prior subcommand (`dk mcp`) and its "flag set, argument dispatch" were deliberately removed in §3.61 — "There is no subcommand any more." **`dk setup` would be the first CLI subcommand in the project** and needs entirely new argument-dispatch code in `main.go` (or a new `internal/cli`-style package) rather than extending an existing mechanism.

## 5. Wizard/interactive-prompt patterns outside the TUI

None exist. `go.mod` has no `survey`, `huh`, `promptui`, or `cobra`/`urfave/cli` dependency — only `charmbracelet/bubbletea`, `bubbles`, `lipgloss` (TUI-only) plus `charmbracelet/x/ansi`/`x/term`. The only "prompt" concept in the codebase is the in-TUI go-to-line modal (`internal/ui/viewer/goto.go`) and the command line (`internal/app/command_line.go`) — both are Bubble Tea modal patterns, not standalone CLI wizards. A `dk setup` wizard would either need to spin up its own tiny Bubble Tea program (reusing `bubbles/textinput` styled via `theme.StyleTextInput`, see `internal/ui/theme/styles.go:200`) or use bare stdin prompts — there's no existing precedent either way. The closest reusable *pattern* (not library) is the in-TUI **configuration view** at `internal/ui/configuration` (documented in `docs/architecture/configuration.md:87-236`): a `field` table with **one pointer accessor** per setting (`func(*config.Config) *string`), cycle fields for closed sets (Rule 132), checkboxes for bools, and validation-before-write semantics — worth mimicking for a wizard's field model even though it's TUI code, not CLI code.

## 6. Forge backends — `docs/architecture/forge.md` + `internal/config/forge.go`

Two backends: `gitlab` (`ForgeGitLab`, default) and `github` (`ForgeGitHub`) — `internal/config/forge.go:12-14`, listed by `ForgeTypes()`. Declared, never sniffed (forge.md:9, configuration.md:22). `ForgeConfig` fields needed: `Type`, `URL`, `DefaultParentGroup`, `DefaultVisibility` (`private` default; GitHub.com has no `internal` — configuration.md:226-229 says an existing `internal` value gets coerced to the most-private option when switching to GitHub), `CloneMethod` (`https`/presumably `ssh`), `Pull.ParallelJobs`, `Pull.IncludeArchived`. The token is **never** in this struct — it's resolved via `internal/forge/session.Backend(forgeType, url, token)` and stored via the secret backend (forge.md:39-50). Host detection helper: `forge.DetectType` recognises `gitlab.com`/`github.com` only (configuration.md:213-221) — useful for a setup wizard prompting for a forge URL.

## 7. Secret backend options — `internal/config` + `internal/credentials`

`app.secret_backend` accepts `auto` (default), `keyring`, `git-credential` — config.go:162-165 (doc comment), default applied at config.go:434-436. The resolving logic and closed set of *actual backends* (`keyring`/`git-credential`/`memory`) live in `internal/credentials/select.go`: `Backend` type and consts at select.go:14-27, `Preference*` consts (what the config field accepts) at select.go:29-34, and `Select(contextName, preference string) Selection` at select.go:76 (order: keyring → git-credential → memory).

## 8. Migration handling — style to mimic for "create from scratch"

- `migrateGitLabSection(cfg *Config)` — `internal/config/forge.go:32`: reads the legacy struct, does a whole-block copy if `Forge` is empty, else a field-by-field copy only where the new field is empty, then clears the legacy struct via `defer` so it disappears on next save. Runs **first** in `applyDefaults`, documented rationale in forge.go:29-31 and configuration.md:26-42.
- `docker:` → `network:` is mentioned in `.claude/CLAUDE.md:463` and `configuration.md:55-60` but the actual `docker:` key (`network_tool_image`) has since been **removed entirely** along with the OCI connectivity test feature — there's no live migration code for it anymore (only the historical note), so don't expect to find a function to mimic there; `migrateGitLabSection` is the one living example.
- Legacy secrets (`gitlab.token`, `registry.password`) are handled separately by raw-YAML-tree editing rather than `Config` round-tripping — `internal/config/secrets.go` (`ReadLegacySecrets`, `RemoveLegacySecrets`, using `yaml.Node` walking) plus `credentials.MigrateLegacySecrets(store, contextName)` at `internal/credentials/migrate.go:19`, which is run "at router construction, before anything can save" (configuration.md:50-53) — i.e., before any rename/migration logic touches the file.
- For a **new** `dk setup` that creates/overwrites a context from scratch, the existing `CreateContext` (config.go:900) is the template: `ValidateContextName` → existence check → `Default()` → clear/seed a few fields → `SaveContext`. Since it currently *refuses* to overwrite, an "overwrite" mode for the wizard will need to bypass or extend that existence guard explicitly (this is a genuine gap: no `OverwriteContext` or `--force`-style function currently exists in `internal/config`).
